summary: ECDSA curve negotiation mismatch with corporate TLS inspection causes intermittent gRPC streaming resets on private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent gRPC streaming resets from serving nodes for long-running generation requests after migrating their private deployment behind a corporate TLS inspection appliance. Sessions begin, generate a handful of tokens, then the gRPC stream is torn down with a TCP RST or GOAWAY from the server. This started after the customer enabled HTTPS inspection on their corporate firewall appliance and deployed a site-to-site tunnel to the VPC hosting their Redwood Private agents.

Impact:
- Affected customer: NimbusAI (private deployment).
- Production model in us-west-2 intermittently failing streaming responses for large generation workloads (responses > 512 tokens).
- Interferes with production feature for end users (audio-transcription+long summary pipeline).

Environment:
- Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC peered to Redwood control plane).
- Customer egress path traverses a corporate TLS inspection device (Checkpoint) in their on-prem datacenter over an IPSec S2S tunnel to VPC.
- Agent version: 1.8.2; serving runtime: 2026-02-28 build; client SDK: js@3.4.1.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) From inside their corp network open a long chat streaming session to private endpoint (POST /v1/chat/stream).
2) Request long completion (> 800 tokens) using redwood-v1.3 model.
3) Observe that stream emits 20–150 tokens and then resets with no final "DONE" event.

Observed behavior / Logs (selected):
- Agent logs (serving node):
  [2026-03-10T16:12:22Z] stream: client hello received, cipher ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
  [2026-03-10T16:12:22Z] stream: selected curve: secp256r1
  [2026-03-10T16:12:24Z] stream: sending token batch id=8943 size=64
  [2026-03-10T16:12:25Z] transport: received TCP RST from 10.0.45.12:443
- Agent application error: grpc: received unexpected goaway (last-stream-id: 45)
- Customer packet capture (on-prem firewall): TLS ClientHello shows Supported Groups list reduced to [secp256k1] (inspection device rewritten extension), server responded with ECDHE using secp256k1. Redwood runtime expects secp256r1 in some crypto path used for session reuse.

Hypothesis / Investigation notes:
- Inspection device is modifying TLS Supported Groups (elliptic curve) list. We see a mismatch between the bridge/proxy-selected curve and what the runtime's optimized crypto path expects for zero-copy or session resumption (in our custom BoringSSL optimizations used by the serving runtime).
- The mismatch appears to only surface during prolonged streaming where we perform a lightweight session resume / early key update for long-lived connections. When the curve differs (secp256k1 vs secp256r1) our session resume path incurs an internal assertion and the transport layer forces a GOAWAY/RST.
- This is exacerbated when the inspection device performs active re-keying or terminates TLS and re-creates an upstream session with a different curve.

Workaround applied by Support so far:
- Instructed customer to bypass TLS inspection for agent control-plane and serving endpoints (egress allowlist to tunnel endpoint IPs) — when customer tested with inspection disabled, streams completed normally.
- Temporary server-side mitigation: increased connection validation logging and fallback to a non-session-resume code path for streaming connections from the customer's agent IP range (applied to a small canary pool). This reduced occurrences for the canary but is not a complete fix.

Next steps / Action items:
- Ask customer security team for TLS inspection appliance config export and packet captures focusing on ClientHello/ServerHello SupportedGroups and key exchange details.
- SRE to reproduce in lab by inserting an MITM TLS proxy that deliberately rewrites supported_groups extension to secp256k1.
- Runtime team to audit session-resume code paths for assumptions about supported curves and add robust fallback when curve changes mid-session. Relevant code owner assigned (see linked GH PR).
- If customer cannot disable inspection, provide a recommended allowlist of hostnames/IPs and exact ALPN/TLS settings to exclude from termination.

Contact: customer success rep: Lina Chen, escalation slack channel: #support-nimbusai

investigation_notes: Lab repro successful: MITM proxy rewriting supported_groups to secp256k1 reliably triggers GOAWAY on resumed streams in our BoringSSL-optimized path. Root cause: resumed-session key derivation assumed fixed EC group (secp256r1) for fast path; mismatch triggers assertion and connection termination. Patch to fallback to full handshake when curve differs under review (PR 2104).
current_workaround: 1) Customer can disable TLS inspection for Redwood endpoints or allowlist endpoint IPs/hostnames. 2) Canary server-side toggle to skip resume/fast-path for NimbusAI IP range applied. These reduce but do not eliminate occurrences.
resolution: In Progress — runtime patch under review. Will coordinate a post-deploy verification window with customer. Permanent resolution expected after runtime PR merged and rolled out to private agents (ETA: 2026-03-20).
